audit.summary: The split preserves the closed vocabulary and responsibility match as linked obligations, including repair boundaries, evidence, exceptions and strict enforcement. No new waiver, mandatory approval mechanism or application-specific restriction is introduced. Mechanical checks pass and semantic review finds no net loss or gain.

parts.risk: Low: the exact segment, closed five-value vocabulary, edit/finding triggers, and six-segment exception are explicit. The strict policy and shared layer context reinforce rather than alter the obligation.

Low: the responsibility-match obligation is explicit, with bounded GREEN repair guidance, anti-relabelling and anti-reorganization constraints, and concrete evidence. Determining actual responsibility requires architectural judgment, but the operative fields give clear criteria.

review.summary: All source obligations, exceptions, thresholds, repair guidance, evidence requirements, and anti-patterns are preserved across the two parts and shared nodes; no source segment is dropped and no unsupported obligation is added. Each part has one distinct obligation and activation. Reciprocal requires edges preserve their joint mandatory status, both original relationships are sensibly remapped to both parts, and the source alias resolves to both parts.
